examples.knowledge_point: Writing a Matrix as a Composition of Jordan Blocks
examples.problem:
$$
[\begin{aligned}7 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 7 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix above. Find its decomposition using Jordan blocks.
examples.worked_solution:
Our matrix can be represented as the composition of three Jordan blocks (one $2 \times 2$ block and two $1 \times 1$ blocks), as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14042906/assets/de67b79aec2eb5b463449cf79735b13e27a3688a42aa26f41ff2157d17c5dc5c.png)

feedback.worked_solution:
First, recall the following:

- ${J}_{1}(\sqrt{3})$ represents a $1\times 1$ Jordan block with $\sqrt{3}$'s on the leading diagonal.

- ${J}_{3}(5)$ represents a $3\times 3$ Jordan block with $5$'s on the leading diagonal,

Therefore, our Jordan blocks are given by

$$
{J}_{1}(\sqrt{3})=[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}],\,{J}_{3}(5)=[\begin{aligned}5 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}].
$$

The composition of our Jordan blocks gives the following block diagonal matrix:

$$
{J}_{1}(\sqrt{3})\,⊕\,{J}_{3}(5)=[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{3} & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$
